findings.highlight: She easily cuts at the man in red.
findings.evidenceJa: たやすく赤い男を斬り伏せた。
findings.governingReading: Saber has easily cut the man in red down before raising her arm to finish him.
findings.explanation: A completed takedown becomes an attempted cut.

findings.highlight: My old man might have been able to cast something with a bit of weight to it
findings.evidenceJa: 威力だけなら切嗣だって負けてはいないが
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu is not inferior in raw power; what may exceed even a first-rate mage is performing natural interference of that scale with no delay.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu’s power and a master mage’s casting speed are conflated and weakened.

findings.highlight: Saber killing someone, their blood staining her hands
findings.evidenceJa: 人を殺して返り血を浴びているセイバー
findings.governingReading: Shirou involuntarily pictures Saber after killing a person and being splashed with the returning blood.
findings.explanation: Saber being imagined bathed in her victim’s blood becomes blood staining only her hands.

findings.highlight: slit open their throat
findings.evidenceJa: 相手の喉を貫こうと
findings.governingReading: Saber is about to pierce the opponent’s throat with the unseen object.
findings.explanation: A throat-piercing thrust becomes slitting the throat open.

findings.highlight: she still holds her sword at the ready
findings.evidenceJa: すぐにでも剣を振るおうとしている
findings.governingReading: She has stopped only because Shirou spoke and is trying to swing again at once.
findings.explanation: Saber’s imminent renewed swing is reduced to holding her sword ready.

findings.highlight: her lips downturned in dissatisfaction
findings.evidenceJa: 納得いかなげに俺を見据える
findings.governingReading: Saber stares at Shirou with evident dissatisfaction while keeping the opponent at swordpoint.
findings.explanation: An invented downturned mouth specifies Saber’s expression.

findings.highlight: she seems suddenly much less hostile
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーから殺気が消える
findings.governingReading: Once she puts away the sword, her murderous intent vanishes.
findings.explanation: Saber’s killing intent disappearing becomes merely reduced hostility.

findings.highlight: her smile has changed into something completely different
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の顔は、さっきまでの笑顔とは別物だった。
findings.governingReading: When Rin turns, her face is wholly unlike the smile she wore moments earlier.
findings.explanation: Rin’s entire expression changing becomes her smile changing.

findings.highlight: I can't stay a coward forever.
findings.evidenceJa: いつまでも腑抜けのままではいられない。
findings.governingReading: He tells himself he cannot remain mentally slack and overwhelmed forever.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s stunned or spineless state becomes cowardice.

findings.highlight: which probably makes her a kind of familiar
findings.evidenceJa: 使い魔の類であるのは間違いない。
findings.governingReading: Her calling him Master and saying they contracted makes some relation to familiars certain in his reasoning.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s certain broad classification of Saber as a familiar-type entity becomes probability.

findings.highlight: magical energy to constantly feed into the human
findings.evidenceJa: 人間一人を絶えず束縛するだけの魔力
findings.governingReading: A mage needs enough power to keep one human constantly restrained or bound under control.
findings.explanation: Continually binding a human familiar becomes continually feeding energy into the human.

findings.highlight: so aren't any burden
findings.evidenceJa: できるだけ魔術師に負担をかけないよう
findings.governingReading: Small animals are preferred because controlling them uses little power and burdens the mage as little as possible.
findings.explanation: Minimal burden becomes no burden.

findings.highlight: Saber is nothing like a familiar
findings.evidenceJa: 使い魔とは似て非なるモノ
findings.governingReading: Shirou concludes that Saber must resemble a familiar in category while differing in kind.
findings.explanation: “Similar yet different” becomes “nothing like.”

findings.highlight: the biggest smile on her face
findings.evidenceJa: 極上の笑みで返してくる
findings.governingReading: Rin answers with an exquisitely polished smile whose quality carries the comic menace.
findings.explanation: Rin’s “finest” smile becomes her physically biggest smile.

findings.highlight: Fixing broken glass
findings.evidenceJa: たった数分前に割れたガラスの修復
findings.governingReading: Rin calls repairing glass broken only a few minutes earlier an entrance test at any school.
findings.explanation: The recency condition in Rin’s beginner-level repair standard disappears.

findings.highlight: Kind of a useless skill if you ask me
findings.evidenceJa: なんとも半端なのを使うのね
findings.governingReading: Rin calls Strengthening an oddly incomplete or middling field for it to be his one usable art.
findings.explanation: Incomplete or half-baked specialization becomes a useless skill.

findings.highlight: Her stare is so intense, I can't help but be vague in my answer."
findings.evidenceJa: なんとも煮え切らない返答をしてしまった。
findings.governingReading: The line is Shirou’s narration after his spoken answer has ended.
findings.explanation: Narration ends with a stray closing quotation mark.

findings.highlight: you run of Command Spells
findings.evidenceJa: その令呪がなくなったら
findings.governingReading: Rin warns about what will happen once Shirou has no Command Spells left.
findings.explanation: The supplied sentence needs 'run out of Command Spells.' Its meaning remains recoverable, so it does not support a claim that the expenditure rule changed.

findings.highlight: I don't know why there's a Holy Grail War in the first place.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯戦争というのが何であるかわたしもよくは知らない。
findings.governingReading: She admits she does not know the Holy Grail War itself very well.
findings.explanation: Rin’s broad lack of knowledge about the Holy Grail War becomes ignorance only of why it exists.

findings.highlight: does that means she really is a ghost?
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱり幽霊って事か？
findings.governingReading: He asks whether Ghost Liner therefore means Saber really is a ghost.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s Ghost Liner question uses “does ... means.”

findings.highlight: a kind of spirit well beyond humans
findings.evidenceJa: 精霊に近い人間以上の存在
findings.governingReading: Rin calls Servants incarnated heroes, superhuman existences close to elementals.
findings.explanation: The comparison to elementals disappears from the Servant definition.

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail is what helps with the materialization
findings.evidenceJa: あとの実体化は聖杯がしてくれる
findings.governingReading: Masters summon; the Holy Grail handles the subsequent materialization.
findings.explanation: The Holy Grail performing materialization becomes merely helping with it.

findings.highlight: Only Servants in spirit form can defeat other Servants in spirit form
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを倒せるのは同じ霊体であるサーヴァントだけ
findings.governingReading: Rin identifies fellow spiritual beings, Servants, as the opponents capable of defeating Servants, then allows that humans might defeat a materialized one.
findings.explanation: The English adds that the attacking Servant must be in spirit form. Rin's Japanese identifies Servants as fellow spiritual beings; her following exception concerns a target that has materialized.

findings.highlight: what kind of sick mind thought to do this
findings.evidenceJa: 誰が、何の為に始めたんだ
findings.governingReading: He asks who began this distasteful system and for what purpose.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s two-part question loses purpose and gains a judgment about the founder’s mind.

findings.highlight: That I don't know, nor could I answer even if I did
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが知るべき事でもないし、答えてあげる事でもない
findings.governingReading: She says this is neither something she should know nor something she should answer, and directs him to the overseer.
findings.explanation: Rin’s principled refusal and jurisdiction become ignorance and inability.

findings.highlight: after to talking to Emiya
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮くんから話を聞いた限りじゃ
findings.governingReading: Rin infers Saber’s incomplete state from speaking with Emiya.
findings.explanation: Rin’s address to Saber begins “after to talking.”

findings.highlight: Obviously not, you freaking sham!
findings.evidenceJa: 当然でしょ、へっぽこ
findings.governingReading: She instantly calls Shirou a hopeless bungler.
findings.explanation: Rin’s “inept/lousy” insult becomes an accusation of fraudulence.

findings.highlight: But it's...kinda weird.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂はいきなり、ワケの分からないコトを言いだした。
findings.governingReading: She suddenly says something Shirou cannot make sense of: that they should get going.
findings.explanation: Rin’s abrupt incomprehensible proposal becomes a curt announcement followed by vague weirdness.

findings.highlight: Of course This is not the first time
findings.evidenceJa: 勿論。この時代に呼び出されたのも一度ではありませんから
findings.governingReading: She firmly corrects Shirou and explains this is not her first summoning in the era.
findings.explanation: Saber’s answer lacks sentence punctuation after “Of course.”

findings.highlight: at least somewhat unusual
findings.evidenceJa: とんでもない事なのか
findings.governingReading: Rin’s shock tells Shirou that Saber has said something outrageous or extraordinary.
findings.explanation: An extraordinary disclosure becomes only somewhat unusual.

findings.highlight: I would prefer that you be stronger
findings.evidenceJa: シロウには強くなってもらわなければ困ります
findings.governingReading: As Shirou’s contracted Servant, Saber says it will be a serious problem unless he grows stronger.
findings.explanation: Saber’s statement of necessity becomes a preference.

findings.highlight: At least that's what I think.
findings.evidenceJa: 偏見だけど。
findings.governingReading: After reading Rin’s grin as malicious teasing, Shirou concedes that this is his prejudice.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s explicit admission of bias becomes a generic statement of opinion.
